result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend explicit modes with a visible mode indicator, undo for Paint, and a deliberate Record. B fits this operator better: it makes Record a one-shot action that can never be left armed, shows the paint value before the operator touches the grid, and asks for confirmation only when an existing cue would be overwritten. A is strong too, but some of its points, such as accessibility and gloves, are more generic advice. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend explicit modes, call out the hidden timing threshold in the gesture model, and add undo, a visible mode indicator, a lock and a test with the real operator. A is better because it makes Record a deliberate button instead of a mode. This means Record can never be left switched on by mistake, the most dangerous state at show time. A also confirms only when Record would overwrite an existing cue and names that cue. B is solid, but its points about accessibility and gloves are less specific to this operator, and keeping Record as a mode leaves exactly the risk A designs out.
